answer: A practical defense is a rate-limited proof-of-stake registry: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can earn reputation or submit high-impact actions, and slashing follows when it violates verifiable rules. One person can still create many identities, but cannot cheaply give each one meaningful influence; splitting stake also splits voting weight. The cost is capital tied up, plus losses for provable abuse—not a magical ban on sybils. A raven may carry nectar in a fable, but neither story nor name substitutes for collateral.
